parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, facility ban, border or custody practice is documented, and the same-sex statutes maximising 10 years are reported unenforced in 2023. That is not safety: a latent custodial statute, no anti-discrimination or privacy protection, documented LGBTIQ discrimination in public services and harassment/violence, and fear of prosecution inhibiting police reporting leave an outed visitor with thin recourse. No documented social acceptance or working remedy offsets this. Thin data resolves to elevated risk, below dead-letter anchors with acceptance and compensation, above anchors with organised targeting or universal exclusion.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No account of border, passport-marker or screening practice for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No procedure to amend markers; visitor documents are foreign-issued.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented. No evidence officials reject or doubt foreign documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No detention, placement or verification practice for trans visitors is reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Not documented. Fear of prosecution inhibiting reporting is documented generally, not custody-specific.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward or public-facility rule for trans visitors is reported.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No anti-discrimination protection on gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented. Discrimination in public services is documented without geographic or facility breakdown.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No information on hormone therapy, surgery, emergency or medication access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sections 430/431 remain in force, maximum 10 years for male same-sex acts; gender-neutral public indecency provision also applies. Reported not enforced in 2023, single source, no prosecution data.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reported non-enforcement in 2023; no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances that year. No legal gender recognition or anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Latent statute is secondary for trans visitors unless used as a police lever, which is not documented; it still inhibits reporting and leaves no recourse. How sex classification applies to a trans visitor is uncertain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule specific to trans minors or travelling guardians is reported.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Same-sex unions unrecognised, so no spousal protections if a relationship is read as same-sex.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented for minors; general discrimination and reporting fear would apply to a guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: LGBTIQ harassment and violence and discrimination in housing, education, employment and public services documented; no trans-specific violence data.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. Fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police for residents and visitors alike.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No documented police targeting of trans visitors, nor documented prosecution of attackers; absence is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or harassment remedy, no equality or privacy clause in 1973 constitution, no constitutional challenge documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: One local LGBTIQ service organisation for over 15 years; resident-focused, not a traveller remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Reform advocacy since 2013 has not produced repeal. Border, custody, facilities, care and trans-specific violence remain unknown, not assumed safe.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar dead-letter same-sex law, but that anchor has established gender-diverse acceptance, no enforcement monitoring, and court compensation. This dossier documents discrimination and fear of reporting with no acceptance or compensation, so it sits materially lower.

That anchor has a trans-specific survey showing majority refusal/harassment in visitor settings and threat-framing. This dossier has no trans-specific prevalence survey, targeting, or universal exclusion, so it sits higher despite thin recourse.

That anchor combines dead-letter law, community role, accepted documents, enforced lodging compensation and identity-based facilities. None of those protections or acceptance is documented here, so it is substantially higher.

That anchor has familiar roles, documented bus harassment, and a prosecuted assault with some remedies. This case lacks documented acceptance, prosecution, or remedy, placing it below, but it also lacks that anchor's specific recurring visitor harassment pattern.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is national only, with no documented subnational variation. The operative risk is not an enforced trans-specific ban but a latent same-sex custodial statute plus documented generalised discrimination, harassment/violence and no legal recourse, creating fear of police contact if outed. Countervailing evidence is limited to a single 2023 report of non-enforcement and no reported killings/torture. Border, facilities, custody and care are undocumented open questions, weighted lightly per rubric, not as exposures. The result is elevated rather than high risk: no organised targeting or universal exclusion is shown, but no protection is shown to work either.
